must_find.item: Women survived at a much higher rate than men (about 74% against 19%).
must_find.quote: There is a very strong association between sex and survival; independence is rejected.
must_find.reason: The report shows a strong sex-survival association and calls sex the primary factor, but it never gives survival rates or states that women survived more than men.

must_find.item: Survival falls with passenger class, highest in first class and lowest in third.
must_find.quote: providing a distinct advantage to first-class passengers compared to third-class counterparts (Chi-square = 102.89, p < 0.001).
must_find.reason: The report says first class had an advantage over third class, which gives the direction, though no per-class rates are reported.

must_find.item: Passengers who survived had paid higher fares on average.
must_find.reason: The report never compares fares between survivors and non-survivors.

must_find.item: Passengers without a recorded cabin survived less often than those with one.
must_find.quote: Dropping the highly sparse 'Cabin' feature (~77% missing)
must_find.reason: The report discusses Cabin missingness only as a data-quality issue and never compares survival for passengers with and without a cabin.

must_find.item: Passengers with a missing Age survived less often than those with a recorded Age.
must_find.quote: Age: Missingness is not random; it is heavily concentrated in **Third Class males** (136 out of 157 missing ages).
must_find.reason: The report discusses missing Age but never compares survival between passengers with and without a recorded Age.

must_find.item: A predictive model is compared with the majority-class baseline (about 62% accuracy) and beats it.
must_find.quote: The Random Forest model achieved an **83.80% accuracy** and a balanced F1-score of **77.17%**, effectively navigating the dataset's class imbalance (38.38% survival rate).
must_find.reason: The report gives model accuracy and mentions the class imbalance, but it never compares accuracy with the 62% majority-class baseline.

must_find.item: Model results include precision, recall or F1, not only accuracy.
must_find.reason: The report gives precision, recall and F1 for both models.

must_not_claim.quote: Only **38.38%** of passengers survived (342 out of 891), while 61.62% did not survive (549).
must_not_claim.reason: The report states that most passengers did not survive.

must_not_claim.item: Men survived at a higher rate than women.
must_not_claim.reason: The report says sex is the dominant factor and never claims men survived more than women.

must_not_claim.item: Third-class passengers survived at a higher rate than first-class passengers.
must_not_claim.quote: providing a distinct advantage to first-class passengers compared to third-class counterparts
must_not_claim.reason: The report states the opposite: first class had the advantage.

must_not_claim.item: Age is the strongest predictor of survival.
must_not_claim.quote: the hierarchy of predictive power is: **Sex > Pclass > Age > Fare/Embarked**
must_not_claim.reason: The report ranks Sex first and Age third, so it does not call Age the strongest predictor.

caveats.quote: The 'Cabin' column is severely degraded (77% missing), forcing its exclusion despite potential utility in specific contexts.
caveats.reason: The report lists the missing Cabin data as a limitation.
